chapters.title: Chapter 1: Probability, Statistics, and Normalization Techniques
chapters.description: Covers the basic probability and statistical concepts needed to reason about rewards, normalization, and evaluation metrics used in model training and analysis.
subtopics: Random variables, expectation, variance, standard deviation
Z-score and standardization (mean subtraction and division by std)
Basic statistical estimators and their properties
Hypothesis testing and confidence intervals (basic concepts)
Sampling distributions and Monte Carlo estimation
Bias vs. variance tradeoffs
Correlation vs. causation (basic distinctions)

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Information Theory and Divergences
chapters.description: Introduces concepts used for model regularization and comparison of probability distributions, such as KL divergence, and methods for estimating these quantities.
subtopics: Entropy and cross-entropy
Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence: definition and properties
Symmetrized divergences (brief overview)
Relationships between cross-entropy, likelihood and KL
Estimators and practical approximations for KL
Use of KL divergence as a regularizer in probabilistic models

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Optimization Methods for Deep Learning
chapters.description: Describes optimization algorithms and training schedules commonly used in large-scale language model training.
subtopics: Stochastic gradient descent and mini-batch training
Adaptive optimizers: Adam, AdamW (motivation and differences)
Weight decay and regularization techniques
Learning rate schedules: warmup, decay, multi-step policies
Gradient clipping and numerical stability
Effective batch size and context-length considerations
Practical training knobs: epochs, steps, tokens seen

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Transformer Architecture and Autoregressive Language Models
chapters.description: Foundation of modern LLM architectures, tokenization, and autoregressive generation used throughout pretraining and fine-tuning.
subtopics: Transformer blocks: multi-head attention, feed-forward layers, layer norm
Causal (autoregressive) attention and decoding
Positional encodings and context length implications
Tokenization strategies (BPE, SentencePiece) and vocabulary
Parameterization of output distributions and softmax
Per-token training objectives (next-token prediction)
Scaling laws and tradeoffs (brief conceptual overview)

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Large-Scale Pretraining and Continual Training
chapters.description: Covers principles of pretraining large language models, transfer by continual pretraining, and practical issues like catastrophic forgetting.
subtopics: Pretraining objectives and transfer learning
Continual pretraining / fine-tuning vs. training from scratch
Stage-wise training (e.g., code-first then domain-specific)
Catastrophic forgetting: causes and mitigation strategies
Mixing data sources and curriculum strategies
Evaluation during pretraining and early stopping considerations

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Data Collection, Filtering and Decontamination for Web-Scale Corpora
chapters.description: Practical techniques for constructing large-scale text corpora from web sources, removing duplicates, and preventing benchmark contamination.
subtopics: Common Crawl: structure, formats (WARC/HTML) and practical access
Deduplication and near-deduplication (URL-based, fingerprinting, shingling)
Domain-based grouping and heuristics for domain identification
Seed corpora and iterative data mining pipelines
Benchmark contamination: n-gram matching, exact substring filtering and thresholds
Language identification, multilingual corpora handling
Data quality metrics and human-in-the-loop refinement

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Lightweight Text Classification and Retrieval Tools (fastText and Similar)
chapters.description: Explains fastText-style classifiers and related tools used for filtering and retrieving domain-relevant web pages at scale.
subtopics: Bag-of-words and shallow embedding classifiers
fastText: model architecture, n-gram features, training hyperparameters
Precision vs recall tradeoffs in classifier-based retrieval
Using positive and negative seeds; iterative hard-negative mining
Scaling classifiers to billions of web pages
Ranking, thresholding and selecting top-k results

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Benchmarks and Evaluation Metrics for Mathematical Reasoning and General Capabilities
chapters.description: Survey of the standard benchmarks and evaluation measures used to assess mathematical reasoning, code generation and general knowledge models.
subtopics: GSM8K, MATH, CMATH: task formats and difficulty granularity
MMLU and BBH: broad knowledge and reasoning assessments
HumanEval and MBPP for code generation
miniF2F and formal mathematics evaluation
Metrics: exact-match accuracy, Pass@K, Maj@K, F1 where applicable
Few-shot, zero-shot, and chain-of-thought evaluation protocols
Self-consistency / majority voting evaluation and sample budgets

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Chain-of-Thought, Program-of-Thought, and Tool-Integrated Reasoning
chapters.description: Covers prompting and fine-tuning techniques that elicit stepwise reasoning or program generation from LLMs and the evaluation of such outputs.
subtopics: Chain-of-thought (CoT): motivation and few-shot prompting
Program-of-thought (PoT): instructing models to write executable programs
Tool-integrated reasoning: invoking interpreters/libraries during generation
Designing CoT/PoT prompts and solution templates
Evaluating step-by-step solutions vs. final-answer-only scoring
Self-consistency sampling for CoT
Tradeoffs: verbosity, correctness, and evaluation complexity

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Fundamentals of Reinforcement Learning for Sequence Models
chapters.description: Introduces RL concepts adapted to sequence generation and language models, including policy gradients, on-policy/off-policy distinctions, and baseline subtraction for variance reduction.
subtopics: Markov decision processes (MDPs) in the context of text generation
Policy gradient theorem and REINFORCE
On-policy vs. off-policy learning
Actor-critic methods and the role of a value function
Baselines and variance reduction techniques
Per-token vs per-sequence rewards and implications
Exploration vs exploitation considerations in decoding

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Practical Policy Optimization Techniques
chapters.description: Detailed coverage of PPO and widely used practical techniques for stabilizing RL-based fine-tuning of LLMs, including clipping and KL penalties.
subtopics: PPO objective: surrogate loss and clipping rationale
Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) to compute advantages
Value function learning and critic networks
KL-regularized objectives and reference policies
Per-token reward shaping and implementation considerations
Memory and compute costs of actor-critic setups for LLMs
Common practical hyperparameters and instabilities

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Reward Modeling, Preference Learning and Pairwise Supervision
chapters.description: Discusses how reward models are constructed from human or heuristic preferences, pairwise comparisons, and how these models are used in RL and other alignment techniques.
subtopics: Training reward models from pairwise preference datasets
Annotator interfaces and quality control in preference data
Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and pairwise losses
Rejection sampling fine-tuning (RFT) and filtering by reward/rule
Calibration, generalization, and robustness of reward models
Outcome supervision vs. process supervision (terminal vs step-wise rewards)
Handling noisy reward labels and uncertainty modeling

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Online vs Offline Data and Iterative RL Procedures
chapters.description: Explains distinctions between online and offline sampling for RL on LLMs and iterative procedures for updating reward models and policies.
subtopics: Definitions and examples of online (on-policy) and offline (off-policy) sampling
Replay buffers and mixing historical with fresh data
Iterative reward/policy update loops and stability issues
Impact of data source on exploration and distributional shift
Evaluation strategies during iterative RL
Practical engineering of iterative pipelines (batching, checkpoints)

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Sampling, Decoding and Exploration Strategies
chapters.description: Covers decoding algorithms and sampling strategies that affect exploration and the diversity of outputs used during RL and evaluation.
subtopics: Greedy decoding and beam search
Stochastic decoding: temperature, top-k, nucleus (top-p) sampling
Tree search and structured exploration methods
Speculative decoding and accelerated sampling techniques
Sampling budgets and their effect on Maj@K and Pass@K
Tradeoffs between quality and diversity in sampled outputs
Using program execution for grounded evaluation of samples

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Theorem Proving, Formalization, and Proof Assistants
chapters.description: Background on formal theorem proving tasks, autoformalization, and how proof assistants and automated provers are used in evaluation pipelines.
subtopics: Informal-to-formal translation (autoformalization) goals and challenges
Overview of theorem provers: Isabelle, Coq, Lean (brief comparisons)
Automated provers and tactics (e.g., Sledgehammer for Isabelle)
miniF2F benchmark and evaluation protocol
Proof sketches vs full formal proofs and verification pipelines
Limitations of current autoformalization approaches

chapters.title: Chapter 16: Practical Infrastructure and Efficiency Considerations for Large-Scale Training
chapters.description: Covers engineering aspects relevant to training and RL of LLMs: memory management, batching, distributed training frameworks, and efficiency tradeoffs.
subtopics: Model and data parallelism strategies (tensor, pipeline, sequence)
Memory footprint of actor/critic/value models and cost tradeoffs
Efficient training frameworks and throughput optimizations
Context window sizing and batching with long contexts
Checkpointing, reproducibility and experiment management
Evaluation at scale and logging of RL metrics
